about: The Agent Client Protocol (ACP v1) agent both SDKs are, over stdio (gap-closure plan items 1.1 and 1.6, 2026-09-26). `webagents acp [path]` runs the agent at `path` as an ACP agent: JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line, stdout reserved for protocol messages. This file pins what is the same in both: the command's words, what `initialize` answers, the error codes, the tool kind each tool name maps to, which kinds ask the client for permission and with which options, and the `skills:` entries the three transport names accept. Python: webagents/agents/skills/core/transport/acp/skill.py, webagents/cli/acp_serve.py, tests/test_acp_protocol.py, tests/cli/test_acp_command.py. TypeScript: src/skills/transport/acp/skill.ts, src/cli/acp-action.ts, tests/unit/transport/acp-protocol.test.ts, tests/unit/cli/acp-command.test.ts. The transcripts both suites drive through a spawned CLI are in acp_transcripts.json.

cli.description: Serve an agent to a code editor over the Agent Client Protocol (stdio)

auth_methods.name: Log in to Robutler
auth_methods.description: Signs in with `webagents login`. A provider key set with `webagents secrets set` works without signing in.

permission.rejected: Rejected by the user: {tool} was not run.

tool_kinds.about: The ACP `kind` of a tool, from its name, lower-cased; the first rule that matches wins, in this order. `execute` before `read` so `run_command` is not a read; `search` before `read` so `search_file_content` is not a read; MCP tools (`<server>__<tool>`) are matched on the part after the separator.

config_shapes.about: The `skills:` entries the three transport names accept, the same in both loaders (TypeScript `NON_LLM_LOADERS` in src/skills/resolve.ts, Python `SKILL_CLASSES` in cli/agent_builder.py). `settings` is what the skill reads back, snake_case in both SDKs (`skill.settings`); every key the Python skill does not read is dropped by the TypeScript loader too, the loaders' own `agent_name`/`agent_path` included.

realtime.about: The TypeScript `serve()` answers a Realtime session on this path (plan item 1.5), as the Python server does through `@websocket('/realtime')`: the caller's metadata and auth reach the session, and the first frame is `session.created`.
